## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T657 (ten fascicles, alt. title 華首經; Sanskrit *Kuśalamūlasamparigraha-sūtra*, alt. *Kuśalamūlaparidhara*) is a major Mahāyāna *sūtra* on the bodhisattva's accumulation of meritorious roots (*kuśala-mūla*), translated by [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) at Cháng'ān. The *huáshǒu* "Flower-Hand" of the title is a bodhisattva who serves as the principal interlocutor; the *sūtra* is built around his questions to the Buddha about how a bodhisattva should accumulate, protect, and dedicate the roots of merit.

**Abstract**

T657 is unanimously ascribed to [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) in the canonical bibliographies. Date bracket follows his Cháng'ān period (401–413). The Sanskrit *Kuśalamūlasamparigraha-sūtra* is referenced in *[the Dà zhìdù lùn](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0005)* and survives in fragments; a complete text is preserved in Tibetan. The Chinese translation is one of Kumārajīva's longer works and is stylistically continuous with the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* group: long doctrinal expositions interleaved with verse summaries, *avadāna*-style narratives, and bodhisattva-encounter scenes. Together with [T656](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0294) (Zhú Fóniàn's *Púsà yīngluò*), T657 is among the major source texts for Chinese conceptions of the *kuśala-mūla* — the "roots of good" that a bodhisattva must plant, protect from being uprooted (e.g. by anger), and dedicate to enlightenment.
